about.title: Suisun City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Suisun City sees a steady flow of traffic where Highway 12, Route 12, and Sunset Avenue funnel commuters and local drivers through town, and public records show 108 injury collisions and 153 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, many clustering around Tuesday afternoon rush hour. When a crash happens, the days that follow matter: insurance adjusters move quickly, evidence disappears, and injuries that seem minor at first can turn out to need ongoing treatment. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects Suisun City residents hurt in car accidents with an independent, contingency-fee attorney from our network who can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and help protect your right to recovery. You pay nothing unless there's a recovery. Reaching out early, before speaking with the other driver's insurance company, can make a real difference in how your claim is handled from the start.

whyChoose.title: Why Suisun City Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but if a government entity or vehicle (like a city-owned truck) was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early helps make sure that deadline isn't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're partly to blame for the crash — your recovery is just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure the insurance company doesn't unfairly inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Fee
items.desc: You're not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can hurt your claim. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover — and no cost to get connected through LawProactive.

items.question: I was in a crash on Highway 12 in Suisun City — do I need a police report to make a claim?
items.answer: A police report helps document the crash, but it isn't the only thing that matters for a claim. Photos, witness contact info, medical records, and insurance details all play a role too. An attorney can help you gather what's needed even if a report wasn't filed or is incomplete.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me — should I talk to them?
items.answer: You're not obligated to give a recorded statement, and it's generally wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements to minimize what they later offer. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can speak with the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Suisun City car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — if a government vehicle or entity, like a city or county car, was involved. Because these deadlines don't extend for missed steps, it's best to get guidance sooner rather than later.
